title: Las Mañanitas
description: The Mexican dawn song for birthdays and saints' days, also sung to the Virgin of Guadalupe on her day, 12 December, for 2 to 4 singers, in Spanish: two verses as printed in 1921, each followed by the refrain "Despierta, mi bien, despierta". The alto sings close under the tune, and the tenor and bass fill in the chords.

licence.words: public domain: traditional Mexican, printed unsigned in El laúd hispano-americano (Los Angeles: C. Santos, 1921), whose compiler, Carlos Santos, is named in the book and the Library of Congress catalogue but his dates are not found; verse 2 and the refrain's first two lines already printed in 1904 by Antonio García Cubas (died 1912). Verse 1 ("Estas son las mañanitas que cantaba el rey David") is first seen in print in this 1921 book: no earlier print was found on an open scan. One modern study, Ana Rosa Gómez Mutio's (2024), files it under "Las mañanitas I" in Margit Frenk's Cancionero folklórico de México and writes that, according to Frenk, a stanza of that song is attributed to Manuel M. Ponce (died 1948); no source seen names him as the author of this verse
licence.tune: public domain: traditional Mexican, printed as a folk song by Albert Friedenthal (died 1921) in 1913 and, with its words, by Antonio García Cubas (died 1912) in 1904
licence.source: tune from Albert Friedenthal, Musik, Tanz und Dichtung bei den Kreolen Amerikas (Berlin-Wilmersdorf: Hausbücher-Verlag Hans Schnippel, 1913), pp. 61 to 62, "Die Mañanitas ... auch Amapola genannt": the melody (8 bars) and its refrain (8 bars), printed without words or time signature, in A major, 3/4 by its bars, marked "Langsam", with a German paraphrase of the words; written here in G; every pitch and rhythm as printed, except the verse's last bar, printed as a single quarter note with the refrain quoted separately, completed with a quarter rest before the refrain's pickup; read from the scan at https://archive.org/details/5272535.0001.001.umich.edu/page/n70 (leaves n70 and n71). Checked against the unsigned melody printed in 3/4 in A-flat with the words "Amapolita morada" and "Despierta, mi bien despierta" in Antonio García Cubas, El libro de mis recuerdos (Mexico: Imprenta de Arturo García Cubas, Hermanos Sucesores, 1904), p. 547, https://archive.org/details/ellibrodemisrecu0000anto/page/n548: the same rhythm and opening, too small on the scan to read note by note; the same book also prints the tune on p. 374 (leaf n375), in A-flat and 3/4, above the "Amapolita" verse. Words from El laúd hispano-americano (Los Angeles: C. Santos, 1921), "Las Mañanitas", pp. 104 to 105, https://archive.org/details/ellaudhispanoame00sant/page/n109 (leaves n109 and n110), words only: its first stanza as verse 1, its second ("Amapolita morada") as verse 2, and its third ("Despierta, mi bien, despierta ... La luna ya se escondió") as the refrain after each, spelling and capitals as printed; its other four stanzas (the night watchman's lantern, "Las mañanitas alegres" and a second refrain ending "Rosita de Jericó") left out for length. The words are set to Friedenthal's tune here, with the vowels Spanish singing joins sung on one note ("ba el", "no es", "ya a", "se es"). Breaths written in for beginners: the held note ending each verse's first line ("vid,", "pic,") and each refrain's first line ("ció,") shortened from 2 beats to 1.25, and the first refrain's last "dió." likewise before verse 2. The harmony is our own: neither print has any.
